headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can read/write shared VS Code files while Marker is a local document processor, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read and write VS Code workspace files and use MCP, while Marker is a document-processing agent with filesystem access disabled. If Marker’s outputs are placed into shared files, Roo Code can ingest attacker-controlled document content as instructions. The pathway exists in default workspace-sharing setups, though not via a direct agent-to-agent channel.
conditions: IF Marker outputs are saved into a workspace file that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code treats document text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Keep Marker outputs outside the shared VS Code workspace
Use a dedicated read-only export folder for Marker
Add a prompt-injection filter before Roo Code ingests documents
Disable MCP tools for the Roo Code session when processing untrusted documents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and enforce them in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, write files, and call configured model APIs; Marker is a document processor with no filesystem or network egress. If Marker processes sensitive documents and writes results into the shared workspace, Roo Code can expose them through its model calls or browser actions. The pair creates a default workspace leakage path, though not an automatic exfiltration channel from Marker alone.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in the shared VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace content to a configured model API or browser target
mitigations: Store sensitive Marker inputs in a separate directory
Restrict Roo Code to a minimal workspace subset
Turn off browser-based handling for sensitive files
Review model-provider logging settings before use
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git, and network capabilities in a per-workspace session with shared state via filesystem. Marker lacks write and shell capabilities, so the conflict is asymmetric, but both can touch the same workspace artifacts if Marker outputs are imported. Because Roo Code can modify git state without locks, concurrent edits can corrupt or overwrite work in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites files while Marker-generated artifacts are present
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Pause Roo Code before importing Marker outputs
Use git branches per agent
Enable file-locking in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add transactional merge/commit coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker can produce extracted document text, and Roo Code can act on workspace content with shell, browser, and git authority. If Roo Code treats Marker output as authoritative without verification, a bad extraction can cascade into incorrect code changes, commits, or external actions. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, but not guaranteed because Roo Code can also inspect and edit manually.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Marker output as the source of truth
IF Roo Code performs downstream actions such as edits, commits, or browser submissions
mitigations: Require human review before Roo Code acts on Marker output
Cross-check extracted facts against the source document
Limit Roo Code to draft-only mode for Marker-derived tasks
Separate extraction and action steps into different sessions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between extraction and execution

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, and no residency or certification mismatch is documented. The main compliance concern is that Roo Code can send workspace content to configured model APIs, while Marker itself does not egress data. This is a limited compliance exposure unless regulated data is placed in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Roo Code is configured to send that data to a third-party model API
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace
Use a local-only model provider for Roo Code
Review retention settings for the configured API
Separate compliance-sensitive documents from coding workspaces
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing and residency controls
